en.title: Split in Order into Exactly k Segments, Minimizing the Sum of Segment Maxima
en.description:
Keeping the input order, split the array into exactly k non-empty contiguous segments, where the cost of each segment is its maximum element; find the minimum total cost over all segments. Each segment corresponds to one week of activities. Added by this site: output −1 when there is no solution, and output 0 when an empty array is split into 0 segments.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: The input gives n k and n non-negative integers. The original has no numeric bounds; this site adds 0≤n,k≤300, 0≤a[i]≤10^9. The cases k>n, n=0, and k=0 are not excluded and are handled by the protocol above.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 9500; 0; -1. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Run dynamic programming over the number of segments. Enumerate the left boundary of the last segment; the transition is the previous optimal cost plus the maximum of the last segment, maintaining that maximum incrementally while extending to the left.
